title: Capability Artefact (v1.1.0)
description: A business capability — what the organisation must be able to do, expressed in business terms, technology-agnostic. Multi-dimensional per TOGAF G189: organisation, people, processes, technology.

realised_by_abbs.description: The ABBs that realise the capability, at whatever level the capability is defined to: blocks attach at the lowest level defined, so an L1 or L2 capability with no children may carry them.

demand_assumption.description: Optional. The demand this capability answers, recorded as an explicit assumption where no outcome is linked yet. Satisfies the demand part of definition stage R1 in place of required_by_outcomes.

open_questions.description: Optional marker. States that the capability has no open question with more than one credible answer, so no consideration is expected to affect it. Satisfies the consideration part of definition stage R2. Omit it when considerations exist.

flows.description: Optional. Named paths through the capability that someone would recognise as a job being done. Each carries its definition stage on the definition ladder (standards/capabilities/standard-definition-ladder.md). The capability sits at the stage of its lowest flow. A recorded stage is a claim; a derived stage (/architecture stage) wins where available.

id.description: Kebab-case identifier, unique within the capability.

stage.description: Recorded definition stage on the ladder, R0 to R6.

rung.description: The former name of stage, still read. Record one of the two, not both.

allOf.$comment: L1 capabilities have no parent; L2/L3 must have one.

else.$comment: L1 — parent should be null or omitted.

allOf.$comment: L3 capabilities are provided by exactly one Platform, so provided_by_platform is required for them; L1/L2 capabilities are cross-platform groupings and may omit it. Realisation by ABBs (realised_by_abbs) is intentionally NOT required, even for L3: an L3 capability with no realising ABB is a legitimate architecture GAP surfaced by gap analysis, not a structural-validity error. The foundation catalogue ships such unrealised placeholders deliberately.
